title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
authors: Yazhuo Liu, Kunqing Ding, Xiaoguo Gong, Zifeng Wang, Yichen Yang, Yifeng Che, Wen Chen, Josh Kacher, Olivier Pierron, Shigenobu Ogata, Ting Zhu
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.
summary: This paper introduces GBClaw, an agentic AI framework designed to automate the complex study of grain boundaries in materials. By integrating LLMs with specialized simulation tools, the framework systematically investigates how structural defects govern mechanical properties like shear strength. The work proves that combining advanced AI automation with deep physical modeling can yield profound insights into complex material interfaces.
main_problem: The core problem is automating complex, domain-intensive mechanistic investigations into the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline materials.
main_result: The framework successfully characterized 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, demonstrating that the defect hierarchy (e.g., secondary misfit dislocations) critically controls the shear strength and deformation modes.
method: The authors developed and applied GBClaw, an agentic AI framework integrating LLMs with specialized agents (e.g., LAMMPS agent) to perform systematic, iterative simulations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on general, asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in FCC nickel. The analysis involves simulating structural relaxation, shear loading, and mapping dislocation structures using atomistic simulations (LAMMPS).
key_observables: Interfacial defect structures, diverse deformation modes, shear strength ($\tau_0$), primary ($\lambda$) and secondary ($\Lambda$) periodicities, and Burgers vectors.
important_parameters: Shear stress ($\tau_0$), misorientation angle deviation, and the ratio of dislocation spacings defining periodicity.
main_assumptions: The framework requires human-in-the-loop guidance for objective setting and result interpretation; the physical correctness of claims relies on linking to simulation sources.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the agentic architecture of GBClaw, the workflow for screening GBs, atomic structures of various GBs, and stress-strain curves showing stress drops during dislocation glide/migration.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the agentic AI framework (GBClaw) to address the complexity of general GBs. It systematically screens candidate GBs, performs detailed shear simulations, identifies defect structures (SGMDs), and analyzes specific migration mechanisms.
why_interesting: While the core physics is materials science, the methodology—using advanced AI agents (LLMs) to automate complex, multi-step, domain-specific computational workflows—is highly relevant to developing automated research tools in quantum simulation and many-body physics.

figures.caption: Fig. 1 | Agentic architecture of GBClaw for researcher-guided grain boundary research. The orchestrator serves as the central coordination hub, interfacing the researcher with five specialized agents, domain-specific scientific software tools, and a file-based hierarchical memory system. The modular architecture enables automated task decomposition and delegation, parallel simulation execution, structured information exchange, and interactive, human-in-the-loop workflow refinement.

Fig. 2 | Agentic GBClaw workflow for systematic screening and mechanistic analysis of GB shear strength. The workflow combines automated exploration with human-in-the-loop domain guidance across six key stages: crystallographic screening, simulation planning, parallel bicrystal construction and structural analysis, researcher review, dynamic replanning, and targeted investigation of anomalous shear responses in general asymmetric ⟨110⟩ tilt GBs.
